title: Ketamine in WWOX-related epilepsy
summary: Ketamine remains a research hypothesis for WWOX-related epilepsy. The reviewed sources do not establish benefit in WWOX-DEE, either for an acute episode or for ongoing seizure control.
evidence: In cortical slices from a mouse with neuron-specific Wwox loss, the experimental NMDA receptor antagonist d-APV stopped spontaneous bursts. The study did not measure ketamine's effect on those bursts. Ketamine and d-APV act differently at the receptor.
Published paediatric studies of ketamine in status epilepticus concern other or mixed causes. They inform a separate emergency-care question and cannot establish benefit in WWOX-DEE.
limits: The review found no controlled test of ketamine's effect in a WWOX-deficient system. The findings do not establish a role for ongoing use, developmental benefit or safety in infants with WWOX-DEE.
Receptor action and the state of the neural circuit can alter the result. Acute burst suppression in a slice would not establish a durable effect or a clinical benefit.
research_question: Can a pore blocker reproduce the d-APV result in the same WWOX model when receptor inhibition is comparable? A time-matched control and activity after washout would help distinguish a receptor effect from transient suppression. This is a preclinical comparison.

sources.label: Breton et al. Wwox-deficient cortical physiology. PMID 34634460.
LEGEND ketamine review and evidence limits (November 2026).
